sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Containerising a Rails application has several Rails-specific steps that don't apply to other frameworks: copying the Gemfile before the source code for Docker layer caching (so a code change doesn't invalidate the bundle install layer), running asset precompilation in the build stage (the production image doesn't need Node at runtime), setting RAILS_ENV=production, and ensuring the master key is available at runtime without being committed to the image. Kamal is the modern Rails deployment tool from the Rails team — it uses Docker under the hood with Traefik as the reverse proxy and supports zero-downtime deploys with a rolling restart strategy. This page covers the Dockerfile, Kamal deploy.yml, GitHub Actions for Rails CI/CD, and the zero-downtime migration patterns that must accompany every schema-changing deploy.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: dockerfile-rails, kamal-deployment, cicd-rails, zero-downtime-deploy. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
